title: Four-register search program
statement: Consider a four-register program with two oracle deciders and the control states listed for the search machine. It starts at init, increments register 1 and enters scan; scan calls decider 0 on the whole-input virtual query formed from register 0, proceeding to incI on yes and dbl on no; incI increments register 0 and returns to scan. At dbl it proceeds to enum if register 0 is zero, and otherwise decrements register 0 and enters decI; decI decrements register 1 and enters d1. In d1, if register 1 is zero it enters d2, and otherwise it decrements register 1, increments register 2 twice through d1a, d1b, and d1c, and returns to d1. In d2, if register 2 is zero it returns to dbl, and otherwise it decrements register 2, increments register 1, and returns to d2. At enum it rejects if registers 3 and 1 are equal, and otherwise enters chk; chk calls decider 1 on the whole-input virtual query formed from register 3, accepting on yes and entering nxt on no; nxt increments register 3 and returns to enum. The accepting and rejecting states halt with answers true and false, respectively.
